gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies the same Algorithm 2 defect: an angular distance d is compared against the non-angular threshold 1/sqrt(n) instead of the conjectured angular value arccos(1/sqrt(n)), causing incorrect extremal/counterexample classification. Its repair explicitly replaces the threshold with arccos(1/sqrt(n)).
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the wrong threshold scale in Algorithm 2: the algorithm compares an angle-valued Distance(A) against 1/sqrt(n), rather than against theta_n=arccos(1/sqrt(n)), so both predicates can misclassify inputs.

component_coverage.gold_component: Algorithm 2 centers both extremality tests at the wrong numerical scale, using 1/sqrt(n) instead of the angle theta_n=arccos(1/sqrt(n)), which misclassifies exact and nonextremal inputs.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that Distance(A) returns an angle arccos(1/sqrt(n)), that the algorithm instead compares d with 1/sqrt(n) plus or minus epsilon, demonstrates misclassification of a true extremal input, and gives the specific threshold correction.
